correctness.rationale: For all positive finite \(r,g\), the exact quadratic generator identity gives a Foster–Lyapunov bound and stationary centering. Diagonalizing the linear SDE after its last Poisson reset yields the exact mean and variance. Palm sampling of the bath state and exponential age gives an integral identity with preserved memory. Jensen supplies divergence of \(\mathbb E e^{sX}\) at \(|s|\ge\sqrt{r(g+1)}\); a compact bath event, Gaussian Mills asymptotics and saddle minimization yield \(\liminf_{z\to\infty}z^{-1}\log\mathbb P(X>z)\ge-\sqrt{r(g+1)}\). The separately defined bounded-variance Gaussian mixture has quadratic log-tail rate \(r/[2(2r+1)]\). The standalone symbolic program verifies the critical finite algebra. No exact finite-\(g\) upper tail or parameter limit is asserted.

value.rationale: The motivating physical gap is whether the strong-memory quasistatic Gaussian profile remains accurate arbitrarily far into the stationary tails when the bath has very large but finite friction. The result gives a quantitative nonuniformity: for every finite bath friction a rare long Poisson-free interval produces diffusive motion of the free common mode, forcing an exponential-moment obstruction and at least exponentially likely large excursions. This is a structural boundary for interpreting stationary rare events, beyond reproducing a known moment or changing a numerical coefficient.
